sentences.text: Background 2. Brief facts of the case gleaned from para 27 (i) to (iv) of the petition would disclose that Gaurav Mishra driving Canter No. HR-38U-3963 from Gurgaon towards Faridabad had reached Mangar Chungi More on 10.08.2018 at about 3:15 am when Dumper bearing No. RJ-32-GB-5128 ahead of his vehicle suddenly stopped and reversed without any signal or indicator causing accident as a result of which deceased Gaurav Mishra got crushed under the Dumper fully loaded with stones which toppled over his vehicle and died at the spot.

It is submitted that road accident resulting in death of Gaurav Mishra was caused due to rash and negligent driving of Dumper by R1/Devender (driver) which vehicle was registered in the name of R2/Subhash Chand (owner) and was insured with R3/United India Insurance Co. Ltd. against Third Party Risk.

Similar ruling has been returned by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2007 SCC Online Del 1700 by holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.

sentences.text: In the facts and circumstances of the case and on the basis of evidence adduced on record it is established that death of Gaurav Mishra has been caused due to rash and negligent driving of Dumper No. RJ-32GB-5128 by R1/Devender who suddenly stopped and reversed the vehicle which led to collision as a result of which the Dumper toppled over Canter No. HR-38U-3963 and MACT No. 97/2019 Anju Devi & Devender & Ors.
Page No. 9 of 22 its driver got crushed under the overloaded Dumper.
Claimants being father and mother are therefore entitled to receive compensation for death of Late Gaurav Mishra in aforesaid accident.

Quantum of compensation to be paid to parents of deceased is required to be assessed under following heads:
INCOME 25. PW-1

Sh. Dilip Mishra having deposed about monthly income Rs.18,000/- in para 4 of affidavit Ex.PW-1/A has fairly conceded during cross-examination by Ld. counsel for R3 that he has not filed any documentary proof verifying education, income and employment of his son.

In the absence of any documentary evidence, notional income of Gaurav Mishra is to be taken as per minimum wage of driver of heavy vehicle in the State of Haryana which is Rs.10,901.52/- w.e.f. 01.01.2018.
FUTURE PROSPECT 26.
Late Gaurav Mishra was employed as driver of heavy vehicle and copy of driving license of deceased has been adduced in evidence as Ex.PW-1/2 (Colly.).

Therefore, in view of the principles laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 59.4 of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, (2017) 16 SCC 680, deceased Gaurav Mishra aged 24 year engaged as driver on fixed salary at the time of death would have future prospect @ 40% upon his notional income.

sentences.text: MACT No. 97/2019 Anju Devi & Devender & Ors. Page No. 10 of 22 PERSONAL LIVING AND EXPENSES 27.

Deceased Gaurav Mishra is survived by his parents namely Sh. Dilip Mishra (father) and Smt.
Anju Devi (mother).

Since deceased was a bachlor whereas PW-1 Sh. Dilip Mishra has deposed about his monthly income Rs.10,000/- during cross- examination so Sh. Dilip Mishra being father cannot be considered as dependent of Late Gaurav Mishra.
50% of income of deceased is therefore required to be deducted as personal living and expenses as laid down in paras 31 and 32 of Sarla Verma & Ors.
Vs. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 which have been affirmed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 41 of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi (Supra).

opennyai_summary.facts:
It is submitted that road accident resulting in death of Gaurav Mishra was caused due to rash and negligent driving of Dumper by R1/Devender (driver) which vehicle was registered in the name of R2/Subhash Chand (owner) and was insured with R3/United India Insurance Co. Ltd. against Third Party Risk.
R3/United India Insurance Co. Ltd. on the other hand has contested the claim by disputing - (i) territorial jurisdiction of Claims Tribunal, South West Delhi AND (ii)
liability to pay compensation for death of Gaurav Mishra in road accident in the absence of valid and effective driving license, permit and fitness certificate of offending Dumper.
Insurance company, nevertheless, has admitted Policy No.
1417023113P100989847 of Dumper No.RJ-32-GB-5128 in the name of Sh. Subhash Chand valid for the period from 19.04.2018 to 18.04.2019 and sought to raise statutory defences under section 149(2) read with section 170 of Motor Vehicle Act in case of non-production of valid and effective DL and permit.
opennyai_summary.issue:
(a) Whether deceased Gaurav Mishra sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident on dated 10.08.2018 caused due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle MACT No. 97/2019 Anju Devi &
Devender & Ors.
OPP (b) Whether the petitioner is entitled to claim compensation, if so, what amount and from whom? ...
21. FINDING : Issue no. 1 is therefore decided in favour of claimants by holding that fatal injuries sustained by deceased Gaurav Mishra in road accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of Dumper No. RJ-32GB-5128 by R1/Devender which vehicle was registered in the name of R2/Subhash Chand and insured with R3/United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
22.
Issue No.2 Whether the petitioner is entitled to claim compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?
opennyai_summary.arguments: Ld. Counsel for insurance company, in addition, has relied upon judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi titled Gurmeet Singh Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. in MAC.APP 288/2021 decided on 06.10.2023 for seeking right to recover the amount of compensation paid to claimants from R1/driver and R2/owner in the absence of valid and effective permit of the offending Dumper.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is all the more important to bear in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible for the claimants who are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability as MACT No. 97/2019 Anju Devi &
Devender & Ors.
standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt does not apply to claim petitions under Motor Vehicle Act as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 15 of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SCC 530.
19.
Similar ruling has been returned by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in para 12 of its judgment delivered in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2007 SCC Online Del 1700 by holding that proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to proceeding in a civil suit hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed and FIR against the driver along with criminal record of the case showing completion of investigation by the police leading to Final Report are sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
20.
Hence, in view of the facts and circumstances of the case and on the basis of certified copy of Final Report for offences under section 279/337/304A IPC & 194/192A/192 of M.V. Act filed along with (i) site plan; (ii) postmortem report of deceased;
(iii) seizure memo of DL, RC, policy AND (iv) seizure memo and mechanical inspection report of Canter and Dumper involved in the accident, it is established that deceased Gaurav Mishra sustained fatal injuries in road accident on 10.08.2018 caused due to rash and negligent driving of Dumper No. RJ-32GB-5128.
In the facts and circumstances of the case and on the basis of evidence adduced on record it is established that death of Gaurav Mishra has been caused due to rash and negligent driving of Dumper No. RJ-32GB-5128 by R1/Devender who suddenly stopped and reversed the vehicle which led to collision as a result of which the Dumper toppled over Canter No. HR-38U-3963 and MACT No. 97/2019 Anju Devi & Devender & Ors.
Claimants being father and mother are therefore entitled to receive compensation for death of Late Gaurav Mishra in aforesaid accident.
Therefore, in view of the principles laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 59.4 of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, (2017) 16 SCC 680, deceased Gaurav Mishra aged 24 year engaged as driver on fixed salary at the time of death would have future prospect @ 40% upon his notional income.
Vs. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 which have been affirmed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 41 of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi (Supra).
Hence, age of deceased on 10.08.2018 is taken as 24 year and multiplier of 18 will apply in the case as held in para 19 read with para 42 of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. DTC (Supra) which has been approved by the Constituion Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in para 42 of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi (Supra).
In terms of the law/guidelines laid down in (i) Pranay Sethi (Supra) read with (ii) Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Nanu Ram (2018) 18 SCC 130 AND (iii) United India Insurance Co.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Having regard to the fact and circumstances of the present case, it will be just and proper to award interest @ 9%
per annum on the awarded amount in view of the law laid down in Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport Corporation Ltd. 2020 SCC Online SC 601.
Hence, claimants are awarded interest @ 9%
per annum upon awarded amount rounded off as 17,70,000/- from the date of filing of petition on 31.01.2019 till realization.
LIABILITY 36. R1/Devender (driver) having caused accident by stopping and reversing offending Dumber No.
RJ-32-GB-5128 without any signal or indicator being principal tortfeasor of motor accident resulting in death of Gaurav Mishra and R2/Subhash Chand (owner) being vicariously liable for the act of the MACT No. 97/2019 Anju Devi & Devender & Ors.
Page No. 14 of 22 principal are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation awarded to claimants.
However, since offending Dumber No. RJ- 32-GB-5128 was insured against Third Party Risk so R3/United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
being contractually liable under Section 149 (1) of M. V. Act shall pay the awarded amount along with interest to claimants with right to recover the same from R1/Devender and R2/Subhash Chand who failed to produce valid and effective permit of offending Dumper despite notice under Order XII Rule 8 CPC in terms of the dicta of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in (i) Gurmeet Singh Vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. 2023 SCC Online 6269 AND (ii) IFFCO TOKIO General Insurance Co.

MAC.APP 21/2016 decided on 11.12.2023.
